name: Bangkok
title: Holidays in Bangkok
intro: Golden temples, river boats and night markets, the classic start to a Thailand trip. Here's what Bangkok is like with the family and when to go.

facts.label: Time difference
facts.value: 6 to 7 hrs ahead of the UK

facts_note: Fill in the Thailand Digital Arrival Card online before you land. Check entry rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: November to February is the coolest and driest time. March to May is very hot, and mid-April brings Songkran, a huge citywide water fight. June to October is rainy, but showers are usually short and prices lower.

things.name: Grand Palace
things.blurb: Glittering temples and the Emerald Buddha. Cover shoulders and knees.

things.name: Wat Arun
things.blurb: The Temple of Dawn, decorated with china, just across the river.

things.name: River boat
things.blurb: The orange-flag Chao Phraya boats are a cheap, breezy way to see the city.

things.name: Lumphini Park
things.blurb: Paddle boats and big monitor lizards wandering about.

things.name: Chatuchak Market
things.blurb: A huge weekend market with thousands of stalls and lots of snacks.

things.name: SEA LIFE Bangkok
things.blurb: A big aquarium in a shopping mall, good for a hot afternoon.

faqs.question: Is Bangkok good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes, as part of a Thailand trip. Children are welcomed everywhere, and the food is great. Use the Skytrain and river boats to avoid the traffic.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Three or four nights, then head to the islands or Chiang Mai for the rest of a two-week trip.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, British passport holders can visit for a holiday without a visa, but must fill in the digital arrival card online. Check GOV.UK for the current rules, as Thailand has been reviewing them.

faqs.question: Is the street food safe for children?
faqs.answer: Generally, yes. Pick busy stalls where food is cooked fresh in front of you, and drink bottled water.
